item.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
item.description: arXiv:2610.19261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Wojciech Tarnowski, Sergey Denisov, Karol \.Zyczkowski

item.title: Understanding the Mpemba Effect through a Rule of Thumb
item.description: arXiv:2610.19870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Mpemba effect, a system prepared farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one prepared closer to it. Its persistence across diverse systems, and under different dynamics of the same system, suggests that it is largely rooted in equilibrium properties, with the dynamics deciding only which mode relaxes slowest. Here we propose a simple rule of thumb for anticipating the Mpemba effect: the effect is expected when a single low-order equilibrium moment is nonmonotonic in temperature. The bath singles out this moment as the slowest to relax, so that its displacement from its bath value sets the amplitude of the slowest relaxation mode. We establish this relation exactly for low-dimensional Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes. We then extend the rule to mean-field models by approximating their relaxation near the final equilibrium state by an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. For the mean-field Ising antiferromagnet, which we solve exactly in the thermodynamic limit, this approximation reproduces the main structure of the Mpemba phase diagram, including strong effects far from any phase transition. Finally, we give a general prescription for mean-field systems: identify the slowest symmetry-allowed moment of the normal coordinates at the bath, and follow its equilibrium value as a function of preparation temperature. This offers a practical route from equilibrium observables to anomalous relaxation without diagonalizing the dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Ran Yaacoby

item.title: Absolute area under a scaled Brownian motion with resetting
item.description: arXiv:2610.19985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the statistical properties and ergodic behavior of the absolute area below the trajectory of a particle subject to stochastic resetting and moving according to a scaled Brownian motion with exponent $\beta$. We compare the contributions to the absolute area from the waiting times between resets and the backward recurrence time. Using the renewal formalism we derive the lower-order moments of the absolute area under both Poissonian and heavy-tailed power-law resetting waiting time distributions with exponent $\alpha$. For Poissonian resetting, stochastic interruption suppresses fluctuations, driving the area to be ergodic, regardless of the value of $\beta$. In contrast, power-law resetting yields a rich spectrum of ergodic regimes. For $0 < \alpha < 1$, the system displays weak ergodicity breaking and the maximum contribution dominates the area accumulated during the waiting times. For $1+\beta < \alpha < 2$, we unveil an ergodic transition exclusive to the subdiffusive regime at $\alpha=1+\beta$, where ergodicity is restored. These results clarify the subtle interplay between anomalous diffusion and power-law waiting times between resettings. Our results are tested by numerical simulations exhibiting an excellent agreement.
item.dc:creator: Vicen\c{c} M\'endez, Javier Crist\'in

item.title: Physical limits to stochastic classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic physical computers use random transitions between states to process inputs. We quantify their ability to solve distinct tasks as the control parameters of a device vary. For Markov jump devices, we bound the number of classification tasks attainable at a prescribed output margin, with each task defined as a binary labeling of fixed inputs. Combining geometric packing with fluctuation-response inequalities, we bound this number in terms of the control range and dimension, rate sensitivities, output fluctuations, and entropy production. For state and net-current observables, when controls change kinetics without changing thermodynamic forces and energies, the number of tasks is shaped by entropy production and output fluctuations. If the product of their maximum values over the allowed control settings and inputs is too small, the device can perform at most one task. An exactly solvable two-state switch illustrates how sufficient driving and observation time enable barrier tuning to select copying or inversion.
item.dc:creator: Timur Aslyamov, Massimiliano Esposito

item.title: Droplets obstruct Onsager-type solutions of the Ising model in a magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.20569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Onsager solved the two-dimensional Ising model in zero field, but no solution is known in a magnetic field. We prove that in any dimension $d\ge2$, at every fixed dimensionless field outside a countable set, the free energy obeys no algebraic differential equation in the coupling, even locally. The obstruction arises from droplet geometry: the maximal droplet volume grows as the $d/(d-1)$ power of its boundary size, while an integer band in the pressure coefficients protects the extremal contributions against cancellation. Our result excludes Onsager-type solutions and closed forms in elliptic, hypergeometric, or Painlev\'e functions of the coupling at these fields.
item.dc:creator: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian

item.title: Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.18892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $d\mu = \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Weso{\l}owski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Itoh

item.title: Optimal Disorder Strength for Approximate Unitary $k$-Designs in Spin Chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.18954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum simulators with disordered spin Hamiltonians offer a natural route to Haar-like unitary ensembles, but face a competition. Disorder enhances randomness, yet strong disorder suppresses dynamics and localizes the system in the computational basis. This suggests an optimal intermediate disorder strength for approximating a unitary $k$-design, which has so far been identified mainly empirically. Here, we develop a perturbative theory for the moment gap $\Delta^{(k)}$, the deviation of the $k$-th moment operator from its Haar value, for the full spectrum of the interacting XXZ chain in a fixed-magnetization sector. We find the non-monotonic asymptotic scalings $\ln \Delta^{(k)}\sim -\sigma^2$ at weak disorder and $\ln \Delta^{(k)}\sim -1/\sigma$ at strong disorder, whose crossover sets an optimal disorder strength $\sigma_c\sim J_{xy}$, where $J_{xy}$ is the energy scale of the non-random interaction. We further show that a multi-quench protocol further suppresses the gap exponentially in the number of quenches. Numerical simulations confirm both scalings and this exponential suppression, and we demonstrate the usefulness of the protocol for classical shadow tomography. This work suggests that strong disorder may block both thermalization and the formation of unitary designs through a common localization mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Gang Zhou, Yi-Neng Zhou, Thierry Giamarchi, Julian Sonner

item.title: Measurement-induced criticality for non-Abelian anyons: The monitored golden chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.18965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Abelian anyon chains whose interactions favor a single fusion channel host quantum critical ground states described by minimal-model conformal field theories (CFTs) protected by a topological symmetry. We show that their measurement-only counterpart, where non-commuting fusion charge measurements act locally on the anyons of a chain of $L$ sites, provides a fundamental example of a non-unitary CFT controlling a non-Abelian learning problem. Mapping the monitored dynamics to a random tensor network, we numerically find $1/L$ scaling Lyapunov gaps, logarithmic entanglement scaling with the chord length, and an effective central charge in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record. The conserved topological charge sharpens with dynamical exponent $z= 1$ and is learnable by a decoder on an $O(L)$ time scale. As the topological symmetry is a non-invertible symmetry of the $SU(2)_k$ anyon theories, we establish the monitored golden chain $(k=3)$ as a non-Abelian generalization of the weakly (Kramers-Wannier) self-dual quantum critical point of the toric code $(k=2)$, and the first of a family for $k\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohui Zhi, Bo Han, Romain Vasseur, Andreas W. W. Ludwig, Simon Trebst, Guo-Yi Zhu

item.title: Instability of Markov chains under infinitesimal coherent dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under local Lindbladian evolution, the growth of conditional mutual information and its associated Markov length scale is not limited by Lieb-Robinson bounds, yet it has been unclear how quickly the Markov length can increase. We show that an arbitrarily short, strictly local Lindbladian can generate infinite Markov length from a product state. We also construct strictly local Lindbladians that converge rapidly to steady states with algebraically decaying conditional mutual information. Despite their long-range conditional correlations, the states we construct are local reversibly connected to a product state by sublinear depth circuits. Thus infinite Markov length does not imply slow relaxation nor obstruct phase stability when suitably defined.
item.dc:creator: Amir-Reza Negari, Yijian Zou, Timothy H. Hsieh

item.title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
item.description: arXiv:2610.19083v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Orjan Ameye, Oded Zilberberg, Jeff Maki

item.title: Kinetic Equations and Turbulence in Large $N$ Vector and SYK-like Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.19130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We apply large $N$ expansion techniques to derive kinetic equations for strongly coupled, far-from-equilibrium field theories with $O(N)$ symmetry. For large $N$ vector models, the quasi-classical approximation holds. Incorporating arbitrary momentum-dependent interactions, we show the dynamics obey the standard kinetic equation, with the scattering amplitude given by the retarded propagator of the auxiliary Hubbard-Stratonovich field. This has broad applications to systems like spin wave and Langmuir ion-acoustic turbulence. For large $N$ random coupling (SYK-like) models in $d$ dimensions, leading-order melon diagrams induce order-one propagator renormalization and finite spectral width. The corresponding kinetic equation, unlike those for standard weakly interacting systems, does not have a local-in-time collision integral. We find evidence for a stationary, scale-invariant infrared solution, revealing a potentially novel strong turbulence scaling exponent.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Rosenhaus, Daniel Schubring

item.title: Mutual Information of Measurement in Conformal Field Theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.19286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The mutual information of measurement of a local operator between two spatial regions characterizes the reduction in the uncertainty of measurement outcomes in one region given the outcome in the other. We study the R\'enyi-Shannon mutual information of measurement in conformal field theories (CFTs). Explicit calculations for scalar primaries and descendants in large $N$ CFTs are performed in the two extreme limits of the intervals being adjacent or largely separated. The results depend on only the cross ratio and the scaling dimension $\Delta$ of the operator being measured, with striking similarities to the mutual information of entanglement. We find a surprising quadratic dependence as $(\Delta-1/2)^2$ for adjacent intervals. This dependence superficially seems to violate the information processing inequality, which we discuss and resolve. We also offer a holographic interpretation of the mutual information of measurement.
item.dc:creator: Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal, Diana Vaman

item.title: How Long Is the Coast of a Neuron? Resolution-Dependent Interaction Order and Computational Capacity
item.description: arXiv:2610.19487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mandlebrot's coastline paradox reframes measurement as a joint property of an object and its ruler. Here we ask how observational resolution shapes the apparent structure of neural computation. We introduce a scale-indexed decomposition that separates the predictive information captured by direct dependencies from the residual outside that model family. Exact constructions show that projection can convert higher-order dependence into pairwise structure. Projection can increase the direct fraction of surviving information even as total predictive information decreases. A schematic branch-to-soma cascade grounds these effects in local coincidence detection, saturating integration and somatic mixing. Resolving organized nonlinear subunits improves approximation and raises effective representational rank. In a nested hierarchy, these gains occur without increasing information about the target. This distinction separates information availability from access by a restricted readout. A point-neuron or direct population model therefore establishes an effective description at a specified scale. It does not uniquely identify the finer computation that generated the observed relation. Which resolution is adequate depends on the observable and perturbation of interest.
item.dc:creator: Nima Dehghani

item.title: Seismology of Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.19602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aging and relaxation of glasses proceed through localized rearrangements that also generate long-ranged mechanical responses in their surroundings. We develop a theory that treats these rearrangements as internal microseismic sources, and thereby separates the direct effects emerging from an event from the effects from the far-field displacements it generates. These far-field disturbances propagate and relax through the viscoelastic medium through which they move, producing a stochastic background of weak but numerous perturbations at any given location. Combining the description of local events from the Random First Order Transition theory with this propagating background, we derive a unified equation for the dynamical structure factor of a relaxing glass. The theory identifies a finite wave-vector and time window in which the growing viscoelastic far-field disturbances can produce compressed exponential relaxation, which has been observed using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy. At higher wave vectors that resolve local jumps, heterogeneity of the local event dynamics instead produces stretched exponential relaxation. The crossover between these behaviors depends on the event statistics and the scattering phase accumulated across the region reached through viscoelastic propagation from the numerous distant sources.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Cao, Peter G. Wolynes

item.title: Maximum likelihood, neural networks and posterior mean for inferring fractional Brownian motion parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.19888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fractional Brownian motion (fBM) is a model of anomalous diffusion parameterised by a Hurst exponent $H \in (0,1)$ and a generalised diffusion coefficient $D_H > 0$. We jointly estimate $H$ and $D_H$ using maximum likelihood (MLE) from density measurements with Poisson counting noise and single-particle trajectory with Gaussian localisation error. We show that one density measurement in time cannot infer both $H$ and $D_H$ and that several time points are needed, which matters most for inference precision. For trajectories, we show that a neural network trained with a squared error loss approximates the posterior mean of $H$, which can be computed exactly at negligible cost. Paired with the profile-likelihood estimate of $D_H$, the posterior mean has the lowest root mean squared error in both $H$ and $D_H$, except near $H=0$ and $H=1$ where MLE estimates $H$ better. In vesicle trajectories from two cell types, $H$ and $D_H$ form a continuum rather than distinct modes of motion. The posterior probability that each window within a track is subdiffusive or superdiffusive shows that $26\%$ of MRC5 fibroblast and $21\%$ of HeLa vesicle trajectories contain both subdiffusive and superdiffusive windows, against $2\%$ and $7\%$ expected from estimation uncertainty alone. Intracellular cargoes therefore switch between subdiffusion and superdiffusion over time rather than forming populations with fixed $H$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel S. Han, Vaishnavi Ananthanarayanan, Matthew J. Simpson

item.title: Single and coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators: Wigner-function dynamics, exact qutrit solutions, and synchronization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum van der Pol oscillator in which single-photon pumping competes with a nonlinear two-photon dissipative channel to produce a quantum limit cycle, and the question of how two such oscillators with non-identical intrinsic frequencies synchronize in the sense of phase locking when coupled dissipatively to one another. For a single oscillator, starting from a Lindblad description of the dynamics, we derive the exact Wigner-function evolution equation, and show that its Fokker--Planck approximation admits in the appropriate regime an equivalent classical It\^{o} stochastic description that reproduces remarkably well the full Lindblad dynamics. Notably, the stochastic approach provides an efficient means of capturing system dynamics in the semiclassical regime, where a large number of energy eigenstates contribute and direct numerical simulations become computationally demanding. Restricting to the three lowest Fock states and using a parity symmetry, we obtain in closed form the stationary-state density matrix and its Wigner-function representation that displays pronounced nonclassical features. For two non-identical oscillators, we study the full Lindblad dynamics numerically and characterize synchronization through the stationary-state order parameter as a function of frequency mismatch and dissipative coupling. We find that increasing the effective nonlinear dissipative strength suppresses the synchronized region. Restricting the two oscillators to the three-level qutrit subspace, a parity symmetry reduces the stationary-state problem to an exact $41$-dimensional linear system, allowing to compute the synchronization order parameter. In this reduced description, results in the limit of large dissipation agree closely with those from the full dynamics, while exhibiting in the limit of small dissipation a double-peak synchronization structure accompanied by a phase reversal.
item.dc:creator: Rohitashwa Chattopadhyay, Vinayak Pendse, Shamik Gupta

item.title: Online training of Echo State Networks to predict chaotic dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.20147v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are fundamentally important from the conceptual perspective of AI, because they provide simple and tractable frameworks for understanding temporal information processing, memory, and learning in dynamical systems. They are composed by an interconnected reservoir whose connectivity matrix remains constant over time and only the output weights are updated during the training period. In particular, ESNs employing online training allow the incremental adaptation of the output weights as data is received, making them particularly suitable for applications in which new input data becomes available over time (non-stationary environments). A key objective in the study of such learning structures is to determine which statistical properties of the reservoir enhance computational efficiency and maximize prediction performance. To this end, we investigate the effects of reservoir topology on learning performance, considering weight matrices generated from Erdos-Renyi random networks and Watts & Strogatz small-world networks. As test data we use the Lorenz and Rossler models in the chaotic regime and the FitzHugh-Nagumo model in the limit cycle regime. In the case of random Erdos-Renyi reservoirs, our simulations show that best performances are obtained for sparse reservoirs and especially when the link-density is near and immediately above the critical point of mean-field bond percolation. Watts & Strogatz reservoirs are shown to demonstrate best performance also for small values of link-density, compatible with the mean-field bond percolation when taking into account the specific nonlocal ring structure of the Watts & Strogatz reservoirs. These studies on the influence of the reservoir architecture and hyperparameters on enhancing the accuracy of ESN predictions provide an efficient framework for real-time forecasting in dynamically evolving systems.
item.dc:creator: Astero Provata, Markos Syroukis, Johanne Hizanidis

item.title: Memory-resolved prediction of ligand residence times on the minutes timescale
item.description: arXiv:2610.20271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-enabled computational drug discovery is advancing rapidly in predicting molecular structures, binding poses and affinities, but ligand dissociation kinetics remain harder to access. Bound-state residence time, important for biological response and kinetic selectivity, is not fixed by equilibrium affinity but depends on the dissociation free-energy landscape and dissipative friction effects. Here, we show that restrained umbrella-sampling trajectories can be used to calculate residence times on the minutes timescale. Time-resolved coordinate fluctuations yield friction profiles that incorporate non-Markovian effects on dissociation kinetics. Combining them with the free-energy profile, we predict a residence time of $\tau_{\rm res}$ = 275 s for the adenosine A$_{2A}$ receptor with ZM241385 (comparable to the experimental value of 125 s) and reproduce the experimental ranking of wild type and two receptor mutants. For HSP90 with compound 18 and RNase S with the S15 peptide, we predict $\tau_{\rm res}$ = 2,169 s and 2,259 s (experimental values are 833 s and 2,439 s). Neglecting memory effects on residence kinetics overestimates $\tau_{\rm res}$ by factors of 2.6 to 29.
item.dc:creator: Hossein Batebi, Lucas Tepper, Roland R. Netz

item.title: Modeling electrodeposition of thin films with compact, dendritic, and random morphologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.20361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We summarize previously published computer simulation studies of a metal electrodeposition model that considers diffusive cation flux, a fast reaction in contact with the electrode or with the growing deposit, and adsorbed atom diffusion in finite time windows. Simulations with various parameters show compact, fractal, dendritic deposits, and dynamic transitions between different morphologies during the growth of individual samples. The dendritic shapes are characterized by hierarchical organizations in which branches of a given order reproduce the shape and crystalline orientation of the branches of the previous order, in contrast to the random branching of the fractal deposits formed by DLA and related models. The simulations show dendrites with maple leaf shape in SC lattices, pine tree shape in FCC lattices, and flower-like shape in HCP lattices, with surfaces predominantly oriented in the lowest-energy configurations of each lattice. Simulations with nucleation restricted to a nanoscale seed show the initial formation of faceted particles followed by dendrite formation, in agreement with silver electrodeposition on substrates patterned with gold nanoparticles. A quantitative application to faceted and dendritic silver obtained in the same experiment provides values of the model parameters which are consistent with the characteristic widths of these structures being of the same order of magnitude of the diffusion lengths of atoms on (111) and (001) surfaces. Using an extended model for iron electrodeposition on Si(100), the simulations qualitatively reproduce the initial formation of multilayer islands, small oscillations of the roughness of a polycrystalline compact film after island coalescence, and instability development. Possible directions for applying this modeling to the electrodeposition of other materials are suggested.
item.dc:creator: F\'abio D. A. Aar\~ao Reis, Dung di Caprio, Sidiney G. Alves, Ismael S. S. Carrasco

item.title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by L\'evy flights under stochastic resetting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of L\'evy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative L\'evy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $\alpha \in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^\alpha$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($\alpha=2$). For the symmetric $\alpha$-stable case with $\alpha \in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Zbik, Zbigniew Palmowski

item.title: Statistical Description of Fermi System over a Surface in a Uniform External Field
item.description: arXiv:2506.12608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A statistical approach to the description of the thermodynamic properties of the Fermi particle system occupying a half-space over a plane of finite size in a uniform external field is proposed. The number of particles per unit area is assumed to be arbitrary, in particular, small. General formulas are obtained for entropy, energy, thermodynamic potential, heat capacities under various conditions and the distribution of the particle number density over the surface. In the continuum limit of a large surface area, the temperature dependences of heat capacities and density distribution are calculated. The cases of gravitational and electric fields are considered.
item.dc:creator: Yu. M. Poluektov, A. A. Soroka

item.title: Hyperstatistics
item.description: arXiv:2604.24783v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a general approach, named by us hyperstatistics, to treat complex systems, in which Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics breaks down at the domain level of the system. Hyperstatistics preserves the concavity of the nonadditive $q$-entropy. We obtain analytical closed-form expressions for the here proposed ($q, n$)-generalized Boltzmann factor $B_q^{n}$ considering uniform, $\gamma$, Log-normal, F, and the $q$-$\gamma$ probability distribution functions. Remarkably, for all investigated distribution functions, $B_q^{n}$ reduces to a $q$-exponential-type function. To demonstrate the applicability of hyperstatistics, we use a table top experiment of the discharge of a capacitor considering $\gamma$-distributed relaxation times, the pressure decay over time associated with the pumping of $^4$He lines of a closed cycle cryostat, midrapidity data for $\textit{p}$-Pb collisions at the LHC, as well as data set for acceleration distribution in turbulent systems. Furthermore, we deduce the power-law-like $\textit{universal}$ dielectric response using a $q$-generalized $\gamma$-distribution function proposed in this work. Hyperstatistics is applicable to systems with inherent non-Boltzmann-Gibbsian statistics at the domain level. We demonstrate that at the domain level hyperstatistics and superstatistics are equivalent, while at the macroscopic level hyperstatistics recovers superstatistics for $q \to 1$ because the Boltzmann-Gibbs character of the domains is restored, as well as Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics for $n \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Squillante, Samuel M. Soares, Constantino Tsallis, Mariano de Souza

item.title: Resonant interactions in the $\alpha$-FPUT lattice with site-dependent coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2605.24268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The wave turbulence framework has proven to be an effective tool for analyzing certain features of nonlinear energy transfer in one-dimensional nonlinear chains. In this work, we extend this approach to the $\alpha$-FPUT problem when the spring stiffness $\chi$ and the nonlinear coefficient $\alpha$ are site-dependent. Although three-wave interactions are non-resonant for constant coefficients, their spatial modulation gives rise to a non-trivial resonant manifold. In this framework, we derive a new kinetic equation that suggests the possibility of substantially faster thermalization with respect to the constant coefficient case. The new kinetic equation includes also an extra term that can be associated to the Bragg-scattering mechanism, which promotes the isotropization of the wave-action spectral density function. We corroborate these results with direct numerical simulations, confirming the radically faster thermalization pathway in the presence of random coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Migliorelli, Giovanni Dematteis, Sergio Chibbaro, Miguel Onorato

item.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For a Multi-Phase Alternating Renewal Random Walk
item.description: arXiv:2606.16339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TURs) impose universal bounds linking current precision to entropy production in nonequilibrium systems. While general bounds like the Proesmans--Van den Broeck (PV) relation provide a broad framework, they often remain loose for processes characterized by renewal events. In this work, we derive a generalized entropic bound for current fluctuations in renewal-reward processes. By utilizing a rigorous variance decomposition within the framework of renewal-reward theory, we obtain a model-independent bound that is not only rigorous but tighter than the standard PV relation. Notably, in the linear-response regime, our bound correctly scales with the renewal rate and identifies a precision penalty arising from cycle-length fluctuations. These results provide a physically informative constraint on the precision of run-and-tumble-type dynamics and highlight the universal limits of transport in complex stochastic walkers.
item.dc:creator: Fatemeh Karimi, Farhad H. Jafarpour

item.title: Gap-controlled thermalization in a SSH model version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chain
item.description: arXiv:2609.09498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In classical anharmonic lattices, the resonance structure driving nonlinear mode mixing is reshaped by band gaps. However, it remains unclear whether a spectral gap hinders or promotes long-time thermalization. Here we study a dimerized Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chain - a classical SSH model analogue with alternating spring constants - and quantify how the acoustic-optical gap controls relaxation under alpha-type (cubic) nonlinearity. Tracking modal energies and spectral entropy via long-time symplectic simulations, we find a sharp isolation threshold when the dimerization strength reaches half its maximum value, set by the onset of the first umklapp process that allows two zone-boundary acoustic phonons to fuse into a zone-center optical phonon; below this threshold, three-wave acoustic-acoustic-optical scattering activates the optical branch on timescales of order 1e4 oscillation periods, while above it the bands remain dynamically isolated. We further show that boundary conditions reshape this picture, producing long-lived sticky states for specific mode excitations. These results establish the phononic gap as a tunable, momentum-selective filter for nonlinear energy transport, suggesting a general route to controlling thermalization in dimerized or topologically gapped nonlinear lattices.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e A. Ak\'e, Gerardo G. Naumis

item.title: Competitive scaling of small-subsystem-optimization heuristics for LABS
item.description: arXiv:2610.14361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) problem, often formulated as a spin-lattice energy-minimization problem, is a combinatorial optimization problem with a very rugged energy landscape. We demonstrate that iterative optimization of very small subsystems of n spins that are decoupled from the rest of the system achieves global optimization of LABS with a time-to-solution scaling that is competitive with heuristics that optimize the global system of N spins directly. Our isolated-subsystem heuristic with n = 4 achieves a time scaling of O(1.333^N ) on the interval N = [27, 60], while the current state-of-the-art classical and quantum scalings are respectively O(1.34^N ) and O(1.21^N ). Our results suggest that specialized optimization hardware with only small numbers of logical spins may be of practical relevance.
item.dc:creator: Ginger E. Lau, Adil A. Gangat

item.title: A quantum annealing approach to the minimum distance problem of quantum codes
item.description: arXiv:2404.17703v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) are at the heart of fault-tolerant quantum computing. As the size of quantum platforms is expected to grow, one of the open questions is to design new optimal codes of ever-increasing size. A related challenge is to certify the quality of a given code by evaluating its minimum distance, a quantity characterizing code's capacity to preserve quantum information. This problem is known to be NP-hard. Here we propose to harness the power of contemporary quantum platforms to address this question, and in this way help design quantum platforms of the future. Namely, we introduce an approach to compute the minimum distance of quantum stabilizer codes by reformulating the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and leveraging established QUBO algorithms and heuristics as well as quantum annealing (QA) to address the latter. The reformulation as a QUBO introduces only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the required number of variables. We demonstrate the formulation using the D-Wave Advantage 4.1 quantum annealer and the hybrid quantum-classical algorithm Qbsolv, and benchmark the resulting QUBO-based implementations against specialized classical distance-finding methods. The QA- and SA-assisted implementations show broadly comparable performance, while the classical comparison clarifies the relative strengths of heuristic optimization and exact distance certification. Our results establish a solver-independent QUBO formulation with only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the number of variables and characterize connectivity and minor embedding as central limitations of its present implementation on quantum-annealing hardware.
item.dc:creator: Refaat Ismail, Ashish Kakkar, Anatoly Dymarsky

item.title: Renormalisation of Quantum Cellular Automata
item.description: arXiv:2407.12652v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a coarse-graining procedure for quantum cellular automata on hypercubic lattices that consists in grouping neighboring cells into tiles and selecting a subspace within each tile. This is done in such a way that multiple evolution steps applied to this subspace can be viewed as a single evolution step of a new quantum cellular automaton, whose cells are the subspaces themselves. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition for renormalizability and use it to investigate the renormalization flow of cellular automata on a line, where the cells are qubits and the tiles are composed of two neighboring cells. The problem is exhaustively solved, and the fixed points of the renormalization flow are highlighted.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Siro Trezzini, Alessandro Bisio, Paolo Perinotti

item.title: Work statistics of sudden quantum quenches: A random matrix theory perspective on Gaussianity and its deviations
item.description: arXiv:2509.09640v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that, for sudden quenches, the work distribution reduces to the statistics of the traces of powers of Haar unitaries, which are random unitary matrices drawn uniformly from the unitary group. For translation-invariant quadratic fermionic chains with interactions extending to $m$ neighbors and periodic boundary conditions, the Loschmidt amplitude admits a unitary matrix model / Toeplitz representation, which yields a work variable of the form $W=\sum_{r\le m} a_r \Re\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ (and in models with pairing terms -superconducting pairing- additional $b_r \Im\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ terms appear). By invoking multivariate central limit theorems for vectors of traces of unitaries, we obtain a Gaussian distribution for $P(W)$ with variance $\mathrm{Var}(W)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_r r (a_r^2+b_r^2)$ and asymptotic independence across different powers. We also characterise the conditions under which non-Gaussian tails arise, for example from many interaction terms or their slow decay, as well as the appearance of Fisher-Hartwig singularities. We illustrate these mechanisms in the XY chain. Various numerical diagnostics support the analytical results.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: The odometer in subcritical activated random walk
item.description: arXiv:2510.05514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the activated random walk particle system, a model of self-organized criticality, on $\mathbb{Z}$ with i.i.d.-Bernoulli initial configuration. We show that at subcritical density, the system's odometer function, which counts the number of actions taken at each site, has a stretched exponential tail. It follows that the expected odometer at each site is finite.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Johnson, Jacob Richey

item.title: The Phase Transitions in a $p$ spin Glass Model: A Numerical Study
item.description: arXiv:2604.15433v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the balanced $M=4$, $p=4$ spin-glass model for a one-dimensional long-range proxy for the finite dimensional short-range $p$-spin glass model to examine the nature of the glass transition beyond mean-field theory. We perform large-scale Monte Carlo equilibrated simulations for both fully connected and power-law diluted versions of the model. The critical temperatures extracted from the finite-size scaling (FSS) analysis of spin-glass susceptibility are in good agreement with theoretical predictions for $\sigma = 0, 0.25$, and 0.55. For these values of the long-range exponent $\sigma$ (which is the power of the decrease of the interactions between the spins with their separation), one might have expected that mean-field theory would provide a good description of the system. However, the spin-overlap distribution and the value of the $\lambda$-parameter do not provide numerical evidence for a one-step replica symmetry breaking (1RSB) phase transition. Instead, our results indicate a direct transition from the paramagnetic state to a full replica symmetry broken phase, with a renormalized value of $\lambda\equiv \omega_2/\omega_1 < 1$ suggesting a continuous FRSB transition, despite this ratio being equal to 2 at mean-field level. A value of $\lambda > 1$ is required for the discontinuous 1RSB transition. We argue that strong finite-size effects and closely spaced transition temperatures remove the expected 1RSB transition for the system sizes which we can study. For values of the exponent $\sigma = 0.85$, which roughly corresponds to a three dimensional system, we find that the renormalized value of $\lambda$ is again less than 1, with no signs of either the 1RSB transition or the continuous FRSB transition, suggesting that the Kauzmann temperature $T_K$ in three dimensions might be zero and the complete absence of phase transitions in structural glasses.
item.dc:creator: Prerak Gupta, Auditya Sharma, Bharadwaj Vedula, J. Yeo, M. A. Moore

item.title: Magnetic domains stabilized by symmetry-protected zero modes
item.description: arXiv:2604.15510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding mechanisms for the breakdown of thermalization in closed quantum systems is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. We demonstrate strong nonergodic behavior in the XX model on coupled chains, where domain-wall initial states retain an inhomogeneous magnetization profile for arbitrarily long times. We find that this effect arises due to zero modes protected by chiral symmetry. Using an analysis based on the Lanczos algorithm, we identify evidence for a localization transition in the thermodynamic limit at a critical coupling between the chains. We further show that antiferromagnetic defects in the initial state and symmetry-breaking perturbations restore slow thermalization, whereas it remains robust for symmetry-conserving perturbations. These results establish that degenerate, symmetry-protected subspaces can give rise to thermodynamically stable nonergodic dynamics in experimentally accessible quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Kos, Dominik S. Wild, Kristian Knakkergaard Nielsen

item.title: Propelling catalytic structures using active biomolecular condensates
item.description: arXiv:2604.27965v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Living systems routinely consume energy to achieve motility, often using intricate biomolecular machinery. In this work, we demonstrate that active biomolecular condensates enable the self-propulsion of micron-sized objects in otherwise homogeneous, isotropic, and autonomous environments. Our proposed minimal mechanism consists of phase-separating proteins, the enzymes that passivate them, and complementary enzymes isotropically anchored to a spherical-colloid surface which reactivate the proteins. This passivation-activation cycle gives rise to a symmetry breaking wherein a single biocondensate is stabilized near the colloid surface, which in turn exerts a repulsive force on the colloid. We numerically demonstrate that this mechanism can propel micron-sized colloids at speeds of up to a hundred microns per second. This propulsion mode is strongly resistant to Brownian fluctuations and external forces. Propulsion mechanisms based on biomolecular condensates may thus offer a complementary, motor-free route to biological transport.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Sorkin, Ned S. Wingreen

item.title: On the Renormalization Group Flow of Active Flocks
item.description: arXiv:2606.20552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the statistical field-theoretic renormalization of active flocks via the Martin-Siggia-Rose-De Dominicis-Janssen (MSRDJ) formulation of stochastic dynamics, focusing on the Toner-Tu theory of Malthusian flocks, or polar-ordered, momentum non-conserving active fluids in which density fluctuations relax sufficiently rapidly to be eliminated as hydrodynamic degrees of freedom. Working in the limit of isotropic diffusion in two spatial dimensions, we perform an all orders analysis of the perturbative renormalization of propagators and interaction vertices. We show that a nonlinearly realized diagonal rotation/shift symmetry gives rise to Ward identities that protect the trigonometric structure of the convective derivative, ensuring that the sine and cosine interaction potentials retain their functional form under renormalization up to a rescaling of their overall couplings. We demonstrate that the freedom to renormalize the dynamical critical exponent in this boost non-invariant theory prevents the determination of the precise values of the critical exponents and anomalous dimensions in the theory, highlighting parallels and crucial differences with sine-Gordon and XY models. We express all anomalous dimensions as functions of the dynamical critical exponent, which remains undetermined due to the absence of a relation ordinarily forced upon boost invariant systems. We revisit and contextualize several claims and counterclaims in the recent literature in light of these results.
item.dc:creator: Kevin T. Grosvenor, Subodh P. Patil

item.title: Gibbs-state phases beyond microscopic symmetry breaking: A phase invariant for the 3D toric code
item.description: arXiv:2607.00134v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Do phases of Gibbs states admit a classification beyond symmetry breaking? We study the three-dimensional toric code with transverse and longitudinal fields that explicitly break both microscopic higher-form symmetries. We introduce the connected correlation $f_W$ of two locally decoded winding Wilson loops. Nonzero asymptotic $f_W$ rules out shallow local preparation from product states. An asymptotic optimization over the observables and physical recovery channels defines an invariant $\mathcal{F}$, which we prove constant within phases defined by two-way local channels with product ancillas and sublinear causal radius. The invariant equals one for the canonical zero-temperature state of the field-free toric code. Quantum Monte Carlo tests the conjectured thermodynamic values $f_W=1$ at weak fields and low temperature and $f_W=0$ elsewhere. The fixed-decoder correlation provides a lower bound on $\mathcal{F}$, so the results suggest an extended region with $\mathcal{F}=1$. Product states, including the infinite-temperature state and fully polarized infinite-field limits, have $\mathcal{F}=0$ exactly and therefore lie in a different phase from states with $\mathcal{F}=1$.
item.dc:creator: Haruki Watanabe

item.title: High-dimensional theory of the glass transition revisited: hopping and local defects
item.description: arXiv:2607.26793v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The replicated liquid theory provides a microscopic mean-field description of the glass transition by combining the density functional theory of liquids with the replica method originally developed for spin glasses. In the conventional replica liquid theory, a glassy state is described by assuming that particles in different replicas undergo vibrational motion around common centers of mass, thereby forming molecules that contain one particle from every replica. Here we revisit this assumption by allowing each molecule to contain only a subset of replicas. This generalized formulation describes particle-level replica mismatches, which may be associated with non-vibrational motions such as particle hopping. We apply the theory to high-dimensional hard and harmonic spheres, where the mean-field description is expected to become exact. For hard spheres, replica mismatches destabilize the glassy metastable state and shift the dynamical transition to a significantly higher packing fraction, while leaving the leading thermodynamic glass transition unchanged. The resulting transition density agrees, at leading order in high dimensions, with the recent rigorous lower bound for random sphere packings obtained by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen, and Sahasrabudhe by using a discretized version of greedy Random Sequential Absorption, suggesting an algorithmic interpretation of the transition: grandcanonical dynamics is more efficient in high dimensional spaces than canonical one. For harmonic spheres at finite temperature, the glassy state contains a finite replica-mismatch fraction even at the thermodynamic ideal-glass transition, thereby shifting the transition point from that predicted by the conventional replica ansatz.
item.dc:creator: Harukuni Ikeda, Francesco Zamponi

item.title: Earth as a Closed Life-Support System: Finite Buffers, Dynamical Thresholds, and Planetary Sustainability
item.description: arXiv:2608.21505v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate planetary sustainability as a minimal nonequilibrium problem for coupled finite stocks and fluxes, using the operational language of closed life-support systems: inventories, flux balances, recycling efficiencies, processing capacities, reserve times and failure thresholds. Rather than asserting that waste is universally more limiting than resources, we propose a reserve-time principle: the binding constraint is whichever buffer becomes critical first. A nonlinear model coupling a regenerative resource stock, an accumulated waste stock and an activity variable exhibits a soft threshold, where waste suppresses growth while processing remains formally capable, and a hard threshold, where waste production exceeds maximal processing capacity. With immediate waste feedback, activity settles globally at the soft threshold; the hard threshold is crossed only transiently or under exogenous forcing. A resource-side threshold completes the picture. We extend the model to recycling and to multiple resource and waste classes, give a numerical example, situate the four-function description of life against the origin of life, viruses and aging, contrast the biosphere's two long-term failure modes, and relate the approach to Spaceship Earth, planetary boundaries, Limits to Growth, System Dynamics and stock-pollution economics.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Gazeau

item.title: How deterministic trajectories and their fluctuations underlie allele-frequency statistics in the strong-selection regime
item.description: arXiv:2609.14549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine statistics of allele-frequency trajectories across replicate populations. Defining $R = 2N_e|s|$ where $N_e$ is the effective population size and $s$ is the additive selection coefficient of a focal allele, we focus on strong selection which corresponds to $R \gg 1$. Strong selection does not require large selection coefficients: in populations of realistic size, it can readily arise from small selection coefficients. Our analysis concerns a biallelic locus over timescales on which mutation can be neglected. Every allele-frequency trajectory belongs to one of two absorbing classes: fixation or loss. When $R$ is large, individual allele-frequency trajectories can appear nearly deterministic. This does not imply that an approximation of allele-frequency statistics can be based on a single deterministic trajectory. For a beneficial allele, the deterministic trajectory approaches fixation, yet a non-negligible fraction of stochastic trajectories may be lost. Ignoring trajectories that achieve loss can produce severely erroneous statistics. We address this by conditioning separately on the eventual loss and eventual fixation of the focal allele. This yields an outcome-conditioned representation of a statistic. In the strong-selection regime, we apply a small-noise expansion that reasonably captures transient behaviours of statistics while recovering their exact long-time limits. We illustrate results with numerical examples for the mean allele frequency and its variance. The biological interpretation of this work is that, even under strong selection, both trajectory types are of importance. We provide a simple framework for calculating time-dependent allele-frequency statistics relevant to experimental evolution, longitudinal population-genomic data, and the dynamics of alleles driving selective sweeps.
item.dc:creator: David Waxman

item.title: Classical Cellular Automaton for Measurement-Only Entanglement Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2609.28743v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a generalized classical long-range stochastic cellular automaton that exactly captures the entanglement dynamics and transitions of a measurement-only monitored quantum system. The corresponding quantum model consists of a one-dimensional qubit chain subject to competing single-site and long-range Bell measurements, with separations drawn from a power-law distribution. At every step of each trajectory, the state remains a tensor product of Bell pairs and unpaired qubits, with bipartite entanglement entropy fully encoded in a classical matching of the sites. This exact representation allows us to solve the dynamics analytically in several limits and to determine the steady-state scaling of the entanglement entropy. We find volume-law, fractal, and area-law regimes. Numerical results show that these regimes persist beyond the analytically solvable limit. Because Bell measurement outcomes change only the Bell-state labels and leave the matching unchanged, all subsystem entropies are outcome independent, avoiding the exponential cost of trajectory postselection often encountered in experimental studies of measurement-induced entanglement dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Will Holdhusen, Bailey M. McAmis, Armin Rahmani

item.title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response
item.description: arXiv:2610.01862v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. We derive the cumulative occupation up to a cut that moves to greater Krylov depth with time, tracking the probability accumulated behind the propagating front. This quantity separates the release dynamics of the finite sector from subsequent propagation through the tail. The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale, while the finite sector shapes the resulting distribution. The early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, while the late edge reflects slow resonances and interference and can also exhibit logarithmic enhancements. Thus, one- and two-site sectors can share the same leading resonance in their continued-fraction descriptions yet produce distinct cumulative occupation patterns. We illustrate this framework in thermal AdS$_2$, where a dressed oscillator yields, in the weak-coupling limit, a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Alishahiha

item.title: Causal memory and structural complexity of correlated quantum sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.06519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: What makes one quantum process more complex than another? We adopt an operational approach inspired by classical complexity science, which characterises structure through the memory required for causal generation. We develop a fully-quantum extension of computational mechanics for quantum space series: Correlated sequences of quantum outputs that do not return to interact with their generator. For stationary, memoryful quantum space series admitting finite-dimensional, primitive causal models, we show that any memory-minimal causal generator can be chosen to produce outputs isometrically, without a discarded environment. The resulting canonical matrix product state representation uniquely determines the irreducible memory required for generation. In particular, the minimum memory entropy is exactly the entanglement entropy across the past-future bipartition, giving entanglement a direct operational interpretation as irreducible memory for causal generation. The same structure determines the minimum memory dimension through the corresponding Schmidt rank. Within this class, we further show that the fundamental entropy rate vanishes, that causal generation is symmetric under time reversal, and that all memoryful processes possess infinite quantum Markov order with respect to arbitrary sharp measurements. These results establish an operational framework for quantifying intrinsic quantum structure, revealing deep connections between causal generation, complexity, memory, entropy, and entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Thomas J. Elliott
